fields: Pairs expected from each molecule's own loss rate — what a ratio value of 1 means in the Coupling-A measurement.

Serves as the denominator baseline against which observed adjacent lost-mark pairs on single molecules are compared, so that a ratio of 1 signals independent losses and a ratio above 1 signals losses arriving together.

The instrument needs this expectation to tell whether neighboring unmethylated marks on the same molecule occur together more often than chance, which requires a yardstick for what 'independent' would look like given each molecule's own loss rate.
How it is obtained or computed

It is read from the sample's own molecules (source: stage_q2_selfref, coupling) as the pairs expected if each loss were independent, given each molecule's own loss rate; the instrument then counts adjacent lost-mark pairs on single molecules and divides by this expectation.
This is explicitly marked as not the law: statistics (a yardstick), and its long-form section is 'not part of IAM's Law' — it is a statistical comparison baseline, not a step in IAM's Law.
Healthy value and how it is set

Its typical value is the pairs expected from each molecule's own loss rate, computed per sample (source: stage_q2_selfref, coupling), read directly from the sample's own molecules rather than from an external reference.

fields: The healthy baseline value that Coupling-A's measured neighboring-CpG co-loss ratio is divided by to produce a per-unit reading; for this input it is coupling_reference_v1 (cardiomyocyte 1.3293).

It is the healthy value Coupling-A divides by: Coupling-A's ratio (adjacent lost pairs on single molecules over the pairs expected if losses were independent) is divided by this reference, so the reading is relative to healthy for that cell type.

Coupling-A needs a healthy co-loss level so its observed-over-expected ratio can be read as a fraction of that healthy base, the way every IAM score is read as a fraction of its cell type's healthy base.

outputs.name: Coupling-A

fields: On held molecules (at least 6 CpG calls, at least 80 % methylated), coupling = adjacent unmethylated pairs over the number independent placement gives each molecule from its own length and loss count (1 = independent losses, above 1 = clustered). Coupling-A = the sample's coupling over the healthy coupling of its own cell type, so a healthy sample reads 1.

Maintenance failure that leaves scattered single losses and failure that strips neighboring marks together are different processes; the independence expectation is computed from each molecule's own losses, so the instrument tares itself against the sample, and the type's healthy coupling removes the type's normal clustering.
Not a step of IAM's Law. Its role for the law: whether restores fail one site at a time or in runs.
The sample's molecules. coupling_reference_v1.json (chain Runtime Matrices/Coupling): each type's healthy coupling from 153 IAM Sequencing Atlas inputs (GSE186458, one laboratory), 56 types.

Band 0.935-1.062 (0.025-0.975 quantiles of leave-one-out coupling-A on 150 healthy atlas inputs; median 0.999). On 30 healthy libraries the atlas never held: median 1.012, IQR 0.990-1.034; 27 of 30 inside (P 0.19 against 95 % coverage); outside: hepatocyte 1.080 and 1.074, fallopian tube 1.069. Test library GSM5652214: coupling 1.379, healthy 1.329, coupling-A 1.037, Normal. Gauge ends counted, not fitted: 0 (no two losses ever adjacent) and the sample's own most clustered arrangement (4.393 on the test library).
Independence expectation counted per molecule (exact, from its own length and loss count); band by leave-one-out quantiles on healthy inputs; out-of-sample coverage checked by a binomial test.

Relay test (2026-11-20): planted runs of losses raised Coupling-A x1.110 (met); uniform isolated losses at 1 % LOWERED it x0.945 (predicted unchanged: not met), because new single losses dilute the share of losses in neighbor pairs. Known-answer runs after each chain edit leave it unchanged.

(1) One laboratory (GSE186458); a second laboratory's healthy libraries are owed. (2) The band is a quantile range of 150 inputs, not yet per type; hepatocytes read near the top. (3) Whether coupling tracks the spread of held error across types (naive 1.29, central memory 1.43, effector 1.55) is open. (4) Coupling-A measures how loss arrives (clustered or scattered), not how much: a rise in independent loss lowers it (x0.945 at 1 %), so it is read beside IAM-A, never alone.

records.name: Coupling-A: do neighboring CpGs lose their marks together, against the type's healthy coupling
questions: Lost marks arrive next to each other more often than chance on the same molecule: in the field's terms, neighboring-CpG co-loss (correlated demethylation) rather than independent single-site failures.
Is coupling just a read-length artifact?
No: the independence expectation is computed per molecule from its own length and loss count, so longer reads raise the expectation too.
Was the band tested on unseen data?
Yes: 27 of 30 healthy libraries the atlas never held fell inside (P 0.19 against 95 % coverage); the three outside are named.
records.status: development (not commissioned); band confirmed on never-used libraries
